Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3056; irrational:--brute, unreasonable.
BiblicalUsage: Irrational, brute, without reason, and Peter and Jude use it for the same men: these, as natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not. Jude says the same of the men who speak evil of what they know not, and corrupt themselves in what they know naturally, as brute beasts.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for brute carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the judgment in it, that men who live by appetite and mock what they do not understand have made themselves like beasts.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; Jude, Brother of James
